study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized cerebellar damage predicts the presence of behavioral disorders in children with brainstem tumors

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction explicitly state the objectives: to investigate cerebellar damage patterns in children with brainstem tumors and their association with behavioral disorders, and to build a normative model to assess individual structural deviations and predict behavior.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text:
Methods This study enrolled 147 children with brainstem tumors... used to build a normative model for assessing individual structural deviations. Furthermore, a behavior prediction model is developed... (Abstract)
This study aims to investigate cerebellar damage pattern resulting from brainstem tumors and its association with behavioral disorders. (Abstract)

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study specifies the reference cohort sources and final sample size (n=849) and reports exclusion due to poor MRI quality for healthy children (8 cases). It also describes segmentation quality control with manual corrections and exclusion for uncorrectable cases. However, explicit inclusion/exclusion eligibility criteria for the healthy reference cohort are not detailed beyond dataset sourcing, and reasons for exclusion are more detailed for patients than for healthy participants.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text:

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and gender are explicitly modeled as covariates in the Gaussian Process Regression normative models. Multi-site effects are addressed via ComBat harmonization, retaining age, gender, and TIV as covariates.
